The '''40th Academy Awards''' were held on April 10, 1968, to honor [[1967 in film|film achievements of 1967]]. Originally scheduled for April 8, the awards were postponed to two days later due to the [[Assassination of Martin Luther King Jr.|assassination]] of civil rights leader [[Martin Luther King Jr.]]<ref name="Oscars '67 Notes"/> [[Bob Hope]] was once again the host of the ceremony.

This year, due to the waning popularity of black-and-white films, [[Academy Award for Best Cinematography|Best Cinematography]], [[Academy Award for Best Production Design|Art Direction]], and [[Academy Award for Best Costume Design|Costume Design]], previously divided into separate awards for color and [[monochrome]] films, were merged into single categories. This was the first Oscars since [[20th Academy Awards|1948]] to feature clips from the Best Picture nominees.

This year marked the first of two times that three different films were nominated for the ''[[List_of_Big_Five_Academy_Award_winners_and_nominees|"Big Five"]]'' Oscars (Picture, Director, Actor, Actress and Screenplay): ''[[Bonnie and Clyde (film)|Bonnie and Clyde]]'', ''[[The Graduate]]'' and ''[[Guess Who's Coming to Dinner]]''. While all three won major Oscars, Best Picture was awarded to [[Norman Jewison]]'s thriller/mystery film, ''[[In the Heat of the Night (film)|In the Heat of the Night]]''. The same thing happened again at the ceremony for films from [[54th Academy Awards|1981]] where the Best Picture winner was not one of the three films with "Big Five" nominations.

''[[The Graduate]]'' became the seventh film to win [[Academy Award for Best Director|Best Director]] and nothing else, and the last until [[Jane Campion]] won the award for ''[[The Power of the Dog (film)|The Power of the Dog]]'' at the [[94th Academy Awards]]. For the first time since the introduction of the [[Academy Award for Best Costume Design]] in [[21st Academy Awards|1948]], [[Edith Head]] did not receive a nomination, after tallying 30 nominations and 7 wins over the previous 18 years.

Due to an all-out push by Academy President [[Gregory Peck]], 18 of the 20 acting nominees were present at the ceremony.<ref name="Oscars '67 Notes">
{{cite book |last1=Wallechinsky |first1=David |last2=Wallace |first2=Irving |date=1975 |title=The People's Almanac |url=https://archive.org/details/peoplesalmanac00wall/page/846/mode/2up |location=Garden City, New York |publisher=Doubleday & Company, Inc. |page=844 |isbn=0-385-04060-1}}</ref> Only [[Katharine Hepburn]] and [[Spencer Tracy]], who died several months before the ceremony and was nominated posthumously, were missing. [[Edith Evans]] was the last performer born in the 1880s to receive an acting nomination ([[Academy Award for Best Actress|Best Actress]], for her role in ''[[The Whisperers]]'').

===Honorary Award===
* To [[Arthur Freed]] for distinguished service to the Academy and the production of six top-rated Awards telecasts.

===Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award===
*[[Gregory Peck]]

===Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award===
*[[Alfred Hitchcock]]

==Multiple nominations and awards==
{{Col-begin}}
{{Col-1-of-2}}
These films had multiple nominations:

*''10 nominations'': ''[[Bonnie and Clyde (film)|Bonnie and Clyde]]'' and ''[[Guess Who's Coming to Dinner]]''
*''9 nominations'': ''[[Doctor Dolittle (1967 film)|Doctor Dolittle]]''
*''7 nominations'': ''[[The Graduate]]'', ''[[In the Heat of the Night (film)|In the Heat of the Night]]'' and ''[[Thoroughly Modern Millie]]''
*''5 nominations'': ''[[Camelot (film)|Camelot]]''
*''4 nominations'': ''[[Cool Hand Luke]]'', ''[[The Dirty Dozen]]'' and ''[[In Cold Blood (film)|In Cold Blood]]''
*''2 nominations'': ''[[A Place to Stand (film)|A Place to Stand]]'' and ''[[The Taming of the Shrew (1967 film)|The Taming of the Shrew]]''

{{Col-2-of-2}}
The following films received multiple awards.

*''5 wins'': ''[[In the Heat of the Night (film)|In the Heat of the Night]]''
*''3 wins'': ''[[Camelot (film)|Camelot]]''
*''2 wins'': ''[[Bonnie and Clyde (film)|Bonnie and Clyde]]'', ''[[Doctor Dolittle (1967 film)|Doctor Dolittle]]'' and ''[[Guess Who's Coming to Dinner]]''
{{Col-end}}
